rejections.standard_title: Articles of Religion of The Methodist Church (Book of Discipline)
rejections.scope_caveat: The Articles of Religion and the EUB Confession are constitutionally protected standards of the United Methodist Church. The Global Methodist Church, which separated in 2022, holds the same Articles; its standards are cited here from its 2022 Transitional Book of Doctrines and Discipline, the only edition published on the church's own domain, and the Articles are unchanged in the 2024 edition. The Wesleyan Church holds its own articles, which the registry lists separately.
rejections.locator: Article IV — Of the Holy Ghost
rejections.phrase: is of one substance, majesty, and glory with the Father and the Son
rejections.locator_rationale: Asserts the Spirit's distinct personal identity yet shared substance with Father and Son, supporting non-division while implying non-confusion of persons.
rejections.chunk_context: The Holy Ghost, proceeding from the Father and the Son, is of one substance, majesty, and glory with the Father and the Son, very and eternal God.

sonnet.grammatical_subject: The Holy Ghost, proceeding from the Father and the Son
sonnet.speech_act_note: The article straightforwardly asserts the Holy Ghost's unity of substance with the Father and Son as doctrinal fact.
sonnet.floor_reason: The passage asserts unity ('one substance, majesty, and glory') of the Holy Ghost with Father and Son but does not explicitly address the 'not confounding' distinction beyond naming the three persons separately, so it covers only the unity half of the predicate.
sonnet.reason: Phrase is verbatim, subject (Holy Ghost) fits within the Trinity description, and the assertion is doctrinal, but it only partially satisfies the dual predicate of neither confounding nor dividing, emphasizing unity of substance while leaving distinction implicit through separate naming of persons.
